findings.issue: OnAfterRenderAsync's try/catch around the JS interop catches only JSException. JSDisconnectedException and ObjectDisposedException do not derive from JSException; if a pending caret write races component/renderer teardown, the exception escapes a lifecycle method rather than an event handler, which tears down the renderer instead of being swallowed. The old code had the same catch, but it sat in an event handler where the blast radius was smaller.
findings.fix: In OnAfterRenderAsync widen the catch to `catch (Exception ex) when (ex is JSException or JSDisconnectedException or ObjectDisposedException)` (JSDisconnectedException is in Microsoft.JSInterop, already imported), keeping the existing comment.

findings.issue: OnDateInputAsync awaits `wakeelUi.getSelectionStart` BEFORE stashing _pendingCaret/_pendingValue, so two keystrokes that arrive faster than the interop round-trip can complete out of order: the older handler resumes last, overwrites _pendingValue/_pendingCaret with its stale pair, and OnAfterRenderAsync then writes the older text back into the DOM, visibly dropping the newer digit. Theoretical on a local WebView2 (I could not provoke it at 120 ms/keystroke over CDP) but it is a real ordering hazard introduced by making the DOM write unconditional.
findings.fix: Add `private int _inputSeq;` and at the top of OnDateInputAsync capture `var seq = ++_inputSeq;`; after the await, guard the stash with `if (seq != _inputSeq) { return; }` before assigning _pendingCaret/_pendingValue and invoking ValueChanged, so a superseded keystroke neither rewrites the DOM nor emits a stale value.

findings.issue: Cosmetic: the else-branch interpolation `class="w-field-control @(Type is WInputType.Password ? "w-field-control--adorned" : null)"` renders a trailing space for every non-password field — confirmed live in the host, where Text/Number/error inputs report className "w-field-control ". Harmless, but it makes exact-class assertions and DOM diffs noisier, and the two inputs now express the same rule two different ways (unconditional literal on the Date branch, ternary on the other).
findings.fix: Add `private string ControlClass => Type is WInputType.Date or WInputType.Password ? "w-field-control w-field-control--adorned" : "w-field-control";` and use `class="@ControlClass"` on both inputs.

SECURITY — CLEAN. No unsafe interop. `getSelectionStart(el)` reads only `el.selectionStart` on the passed reference; `setInputValue(el, value, caret)` writes only `el.value` on that same reference and clamps the caret with Math.max/Math.min before setSelectionRange. Neither takes a selector, an id, or any string that is evaluated; there is no eval, no innerHTML, no document-wide query, and no way for a caller to reach an element other than the `_dateRef` ElementReference the component owns. Removing setCaretPosition reduced the interop surface. Nothing secret passes through: the password field uses the plain OnInputAsync path and never touches the JS helpers, and no password, key or seed reaches a log, the DB or UI state. The XML doc comments are accurate and in English, as are all identifiers.

TESTS ASSERT REAL BEHAVIOUR. No tautologies. The three date-interop tests assert the exact emitted value AND the exact (value, caret) argument pair of the setInputValue invocation: ("", 0) for the null-value first rejected keystroke, ("12", 2) for a rejected character after two digits, ("12/50/9", 4) for middle insertion, ("1", 1) for the second rejected keystroke on an unbound field. Each of those numbers is falsifiable and I independently reproduced the "12/50/9"/caret-4 pair in the live host. getSelectionStart is stubbed to a specific value per test rather than left loose, so CaretForDigitCount/CountDigitsBefore are genuinely exercised. Warnings-as-errors clean on both projects that compile.
